findings.title: Federated rule groups are no longer treated as immutable
findings.body: useAllAlertRuleAbilities used to check isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group) before deciding whether update, delete, pause, etc. were supported. After this change it delegates to useAllRulerRuleAbilities, which only receives a RulerRuleDTO and a group identifier, and now hardcodes isFederated = false. As a result, federated rule groups can be reported as editable/removable when datasource/folder permissions allow, breaking the previous immutability guard for federated rules.

findings.title: Missing key prop on GrafanaRuleListItem in filtered rule list
findings.body: In the rules.map branch for origin === 'grafana', the newly rendered GrafanaRuleListItem has no key prop, while the other branches use key={key}. Since this is a React list, the missing key causes index-based reconciliation, which can reuse component state such as open menus or focus for the wrong rule as the list changes and triggers React warnings. Pass key={key} to GrafanaRuleListItem.

findings.title: Silence drawer never opens for prom-only Grafana rules
findings.body: GrafanaRuleListItem now renders RuleActionsButtons with only promRule, so rule is undefined. The AlertRuleMenu can show the Silence notifications item based on the promRule ability, and handleSilence sets showSilenceDrawer to true, but this line only renders SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer when rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule) is true. With rule undefined, clicking Silence does nothing in the new list view. The condition and drawer data need to support the promRule-only path.

findings.title: Pause action is missing for Grafana rules in the alert list view
findings.body: canPause is now computed from useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities when only promRule is available, but the pause menu item is still gated on rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule) and passes rulerRule to MenuItemPauseRule. In the prom-only alert list view rulerRule is undefined, so the pause action never renders even when canPause is true. Use a pause item that accepts GrafanaPromRuleDTO or derive the required data from promRule, or remove the promRule pause ability if pause is intentionally unsupported.

findings.title: Delete action is missing for Grafana rules in the alert list view
findings.body: The Delete Menu.Item is still wrapped in {canDelete && rulerRule && ...}. In the new prom-only alert list view rulerRule is undefined, so Delete never appears even when useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities reports delete as supported and allowed. The actual delete handler passed from RuleActionsButtons already uses only the identifier and groupIdentifier, so the rulerRule guard appears unnecessary and removes delete functionality from the list view.

findings.title: Duplicate action can appear for data source rules based on Grafana create permission
findings.body: For a non-Grafana promRule, AlertRuleMenu passes skipToken to useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities. However, skipToken is mapped to undefined, and useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(undefined) returns Duplicate as supported with getRulesPermissions('grafana').create as the allowed permission. Because canDuplicate ORs that result with the ruler ability, a data source rule can show the Duplicate menu item even if the user lacks the external write permission required for that rule. This is a UI authorization regression; the backend may still reject the action.

findings.title: View link no longer preserves returnTo
findings.body: The removed GrafanaRuleLoader created the rule view URL with { returnTo: createReturnTo() }. The new GrafanaRuleListItem builds the same /alerting/grafana/${uid}/view URL without returnTo, so navigating from the alert list to a rule and then using in-app back/return controls may no longer return to the previous filtered list. Add returnTo back if list navigation should be preserved.
